additional_info.subject: RE: ID0367674-DC/Si-D/BE-[MP / PD 170001339] Contactor issue CRM:00643000778
additional_info.body:
Hi Marnic,
I hope this email finds you well.
Regarding your issue with the contactors triggering the message, it doesn't seem to be a problem as of now. This error is self-explanatory and resolves itself. According to the logs, it occurs only for a few seconds before resolving. Currently, there is no issue with the contactors, and all the outlets are ready for charging. If there were an issue, the PLC error flags would be triggered, indicating that the coil is stuck, which would be permanently logged in the SCB. It does not seem to be causing any issues in the charging sessions. Only when a charging session is aborted does it give an 'Abnormal' error, which goes away automatically in a fraction of a second.
Please let us know if you have any further queries. If not, we shall close this ticket.
Thank you.
With best regards,
eMobility Tech Support Team -
Shrey

additional_info.subject: RE: ID0367674-DC/Si-D/BE-[MP / PD 170001339] Contactor issue CRM:00643000778
additional_info.body:
Dear Marnic,
I hope all is well with you. I'm Sambath, and I'll be supporting you on this case from expert team. Please be aware that I have completed analysis on this charger for the last month and understand there is an issue with the DC1 connector. Out of 57 charging sessions, approx. 32 of them are interrupting with cable temperature plausibility errors. It is clear from the logs that the connector is not working properly at high charging current (above 250 A). can we have a call today to understand more about the background of the issue?
With best regards,
eMobility Tech Support Team -
Sambath.K.S

additional_info.subject: RE: ID0367674-DC/Si-D/BE-[MP / PD 170001339] Contactor issue CRM:00643000778
additional_info.body:
Hello Sambath
Indeed we discovered this problem also during the intervention with the contactor issue. For now the contactor issue is solved, problem here was a faulty transducer on DC1 which gave with no charging session 14V. Someone from lvl 2 support already did an investigation on the cable and PT1 is giving wrong temperature readings. Cable is ordered.
Br.
